Header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Verdant), Priya Desai (Lead ML Eng, Verdant), Alex Gomez (Platform Eng, Verdant)

--- Auto-summary (auto):
POC scoping for Verdant Analytics to validate Redwood integration for their extraction/analysis pipelines. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost, structured output accuracy), workload sizing, benchmark plan and timelines. Integration topics: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, JSON structured output. Next: Redwood to send POC plan, security docs, and benchmark scripts; Verdant to provide datasets and SLOs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I think we have about 50 minutes. quick intros?
[00:05] Liam: yeah Liam O'Connor, CTO at Verdant. thanks for setting this up.
[00:07] Priya: Priya here, lead ML engineer. we'll own model integration.
[00:09] Alex: Alex platform eng, i'll handle network and infra stuff.
[00:12] Jordan: great, Maya quick intro?
[00:13] Maya: maya singh, solutions engineer at Redwood. i'll run the benchmark with you and help with SDKs.
[00:18] Jordan: cool, so goal for today is to scope a 4-week POC, agree success criteria, get workload sizes and plan benchs. feel free to interrupt.

[00:40] Liam: high level, we want an LLM-powered extraction layer for our financial docs pipeline. need structured json output, ability to call downstream tools, and low lat for interactive UIs.
[00:50] Priya: we also need to confirm data residency and KMS integration for customer data. SOC2 is a must.
[01:05] Maya: totally. Redwood supports private deployments and VPC peering; we also have hosted with encryption at rest and KMS integration. i can share SOC2 + security whitepaper after this call.
[01:25] Alex: ok network wise, if we do private we need firewall rules and dedicated route. will check with infra team on ip whitelisting.

[01:45] Jordan: let's capture success criteria. what would success look like at the end of the POC?
[01:50] Liam: three things: 1) 95% extraction accuracy on key fields, 2) median response latency under 250ms for 512-token requests, and 3) sustainable cost under our threshold - roughly $0.50 per 1k user interactions.
[02:12] Priya: add: ability to produce strict JSON schema outputs with deterministic keys, and function/tool calling so the model can emit operations like update_db or call_enrich.
[02:30] Maya: good. Redwood supports structured output via json_schema and function-calling compatible with OpenAI-style endpoints. small note: function calling is best-effort and sometimes transcript shows the model framing as text, so we'll include validation steps.

[02:55] Liam: can you clarify "OpenAI-compatible endpoints"? we want minimal code change to swap from OpenAI to Redwood.
[03:05] Jordan: yes, our REST and SDKs implement an OpenAI-compatible surface. you can point existing clients at our endpoint with small config changes; we've added compatibility layers for function-calls and streaming.
[03:20] Priya: and SDKs in python/node?
[03:23] Maya: python, node, go - all have parity for chat, completions, embeddings, and function-tool calls. we'll share code snippets in the POC repo.

[03:40] Alex: how about auth + API keys for POC vs dedicated? any SSO?
[03:45] Jordan: for POC, API keys suffice. for dedicated/private we support SAML SSO and enterprise identity. keys for bench runs will be time-limited.

[04:05] Priya: workload sizing - we expect peak of 200 qps for inference across our fleet during business hours, average 40 qps. typical request size ~350 tokens in, 700 out.
[04:25] Maya: ok that's helpful. for the benchmark we'll simulate 200 qps bursts and sustained 40 qps. we'll also test long-context behavior at 2k token windows.
[04:40] Jordan: recommended POC approach: week1 integration + smoke tests, week2 baseline benchmarks (hosted on Redwood dev cluster), week3 optimization (batching, caching, quantize model variant), week4 wrap-up, SLA review and pilot decision.

[05:05] Liam: regarding models - we want to try an open model + a tuned variant. can you run both hosted and dedicated variants to compare latency/cost?
[05:15] Maya: yes, we can provision a dedicated pool for the POC for more stable throughput; otherwise hosted may vary. we'll measure latency p50/p95 and cost-per-1k-tokens.
[05:30] Priya: what about KV cache and prefix caching - important for our conversational flows.
[05:35] Maya: we support KV cache. minor transcription note: sometimes kv cache is transcribed as "K-V cash" in our logs, ha. caching will be part of the optimization pass in week3.

[05:50] Alex: security - you mentioned KMS earlier. do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:55] Jordan: yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer Redwood-managed KMS and can support BYOK on dedicated contracts. we'll include specific contract language in the security packet.

[06:15] Liam: for the structured output, we need strict validation: if model emits malformed JSON we want deterministic fallback. is that part of the platform?
[06:25] Maya: we have structured output helpers and can run schema validation client-side; we also recommend using function-calling + response schemas to increase determinism. we'll include a small validator in the POC repo.

[06:45] Priya: bench metrics - we want p50 and p95 latency, tokens/sec, error rate, and extraction F1. how will you measure accuracy?
[06:55] Maya: we'll run a labeled holdout set you provide to compute precision/recall/F1 for the extraction fields. for latency we'll capture end-to-end times including network.

[07:10] Alex: will you run tests from our VPC or from your hosted region? network will matter a lot for latency comparison.
[07:18] Jordan: both. we'll do hosted runs from Redwood's region to show baseline; then if you provision access we'll run a VPC-attached run or private deployment to measure intra-VPC latency.

[07:35] Liam: timeline - if we sign off on the POC plan today when can we start?
[07:40] Jordan: we can start as early as 2026-09-22. provision and keys day 1, integration week, bench week after.

[07:50] Priya: ok sample datasets - we'll provide 2k labeled documents for initial accuracy tests and a 10k unlabeled corpus to run throughput tests.
[07:58] Maya: perfect. please put them in a shared S3 bucket and share read-only creds; we'll use those in benchmark runs.

[08:15] Liam: any gotchas switching from an OpenAI SDK? function signatures, streaming, etc?
[08:20] Maya: most clients will be drop-in; the main differences are: our model catalog names differ and we have extra params for batching/quantization; also our function-calling returns a combined event payload that sometimes needs small parsing tweaks. we'll put sample diff patch in the repo.

[08:45] Priya: what about cost controls during the POC? we don't want runaway spend.
[08:50] Jordan: we'll enable quota limits and alerts; plus we'll cap the dedicated pool and can enforce per-route quotas.

[09:05] Alex: for the benchmark script - will you provide the harness or do we run locally?
[09:10] Maya: we'll provide a harness (python load runner + node snippets) that you can run in your env or we can run from ours. harness will produce the latency and accuracy reports and a CSV we can share.

[09:30] Liam: ok let's talk deliverables: what do you need from Verdant?
[09:35] Priya: list them out?
[09:36] Jordan: sure: 1) sample datasets (2k labeled, 10k unlabeled), 2) expected traffic profile (peak/sustained qps, token sizes), 3) network constraints (VPC, ip lists), 4) success criteria thresholds (latency, accuracy, cost).
[09:55] Priya: we'll get that to you by 2026-09-21.

[10:10] Maya: action recap: i'll produce benchmark plan and scripts; Jordan will send formal POC plan + pricing; we'll share SOC2 and security docs; Verdant provides datasets and infra details.

[10:30] Liam: sounds good. one more question on model quantization - will that affect accuracy for extraction tasks?
[10:36] Maya: sometimes small accuracy delta; we'll quantify that in week3 when we try int8/int4 variants and include rollback to full-precision if needed.

[10:55] Jordan: great. any other concerns?
[11:00] Alex: just firewall and egress cost - we'll confirm with infra.

[11:05] Priya: nothing else. thanks everyone.

[11:10] Jordan: ok final recap of next steps - Jordan send POC doc by Mon 9/20, Maya share bench scripts by Wed 9/22, Verdant to upload datasets by 9/21, schedule bench on Thu 9/23.
[11:30] Liam: confirmed. thanks.
[11:35] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links. bye.

--- End transcript
